steps.title: Import TypeScript types and utilities

successCriteria: Record is imported from 'typescript' and URLSearchParams is available globally.

steps.title: Create the main parser function signature
steps.instruction: Declare a function named 'parseUrlParams' that takes a generic type parameter 'T' constrained by the 'URLParams' interface, and returns a value of type 'T'.
steps.hint: Use the 'function' keyword or arrow function syntax. The generic parameter should extend 'URLParams' to ensure it matches our interface.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function signature for parseUrlParams is defined with TypeScript generics and proper return type.
successCriteria: The parseUrlParams function is declared with a generic type parameter 'T extends URLParams' and returns type 'T'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly declared the parseUrlParams function with proper TypeScript generics.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the function has a generic type parameter that extends URLParams and returns type T.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature doesn't match the requirements. It needs a generic type parameter constrained by URLParams and should return type T.

steps.title: Initialize URLSearchParams object
steps.instruction: Inside the parseUrlParams function, create a URLSearchParams instance from the input URL string.
steps.hint: Use the URLSearchParams constructor with the URL's search string. You can get it by creating a new URL object or extracting the query string directly.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parseUrlParams function now has a URLSearchParams instance ready to extract query parameters.
successCriteria: A URLSearchParams object is created inside the parseUrlParams function using the input URL string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a URLSearchParams instance from the URL string. This gives us access to the query parameters.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're creating the URLSearchParams object correctly from the URL string parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The URLSearchParams instance wasn't created properly. Remember to use the URL string parameter to extract the query parameters.

steps.title: Create result object with initial values
steps.instruction: Inside the parseUrlParams function, create a result variable initialized as an empty object using the Record utility type, typed to match the generic parameter T.
steps.hint: Use Record<keyof T, string> to create an object type with the same keys as T, then initialize it as empty.
steps.expectedOutcome: The result variable is declared and initialized as an empty object with the correct Record type.
successCriteria: A result variable is created inside the function, typed as Record<keyof T, string> and initialized as an empty object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've initialized a typed result object that will hold our parsed URL parameters.

steps.title: Iterate through parameter definitions
steps.instruction: Inside the parseUrlParams function, add a for...of loop that iterates through Object.entries of the generic type parameter T to access each parameter name and type.
steps.hint: Use Object.entries with the generic type T to get key-value pairs, then destructure them in the loop.
steps.expectedOutcome: The function now has a loop that will iterate through each parameter definition from the generic type T.
successCriteria: A for...of loop using Object.entries(T) is added inside the function body.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the iteration logic to process each parameter definition.

steps.instruction: Inside the iteration loop, extract the current parameter's value from the URLSearchParams object.
steps.hint: Use the .get() method on the URLSearchParams instance, passing the current parameter name as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The loop now retrieves each parameter's value from the URL search parameters.
successCriteria: The .get() method is called on the URLSearchParams instance with the current parameter name.

steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, add conditional logic to convert the extracted string value to its defined type (number, boolean, or string) before assigning it to the result object.
steps.hint: Use typeof checks or type guards to determine the target type and convert the string value appropriately. For numbers, use parseFloat or Number(); for booleans, check if the string equals 'true'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The parseUrlParams function now includes logic to convert URL parameter string values to their appropriate types (number, boolean, or string) based on the generic type T.
successCriteria: Conditional type conversion logic is implemented inside the for loop, handling number, boolean, and string conversions appropriately.

steps.title: Assign converted value to result
steps.instruction: Inside the for loop, assign the converted value to the corresponding property in the result object.
steps.hint: Use bracket notation to assign the value to the result object using the parameter name as the key.
steps.expectedOutcome: The result object will now contain properly typed values for each URL parameter.
